analysis:
The PR is a documentation-only change to docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md. It adds one table row, "Active-store victim selection" (head line 375, the only changed range). The row describes the eviction victim-selection algorithm in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest and SSDBlockIndex.oldestFirstSnapshot: a linear oldest probe with a lexicographic tag tie-break, and a binary-heap snapshot fallback for busy or undeletable candidates. It also records pass-termination behavior: external-removal reconciliation stops the pass, and a closed store is never reopened.

The patch excerpt is truncated, but the range map is complete and shows only line 375 changed. I examined that row and the surrounding unchanged table rows against T-041 and the TB-007 cache-storage threats.

The row is consistent with the existing description of per-file removals under the removal lock and epoch ownership. It does not alter the TTL (still 1800s), the HMAC name derivation, the DBK3 AAD, the KEK purge points or the disk-budget policy, so the SEC-035 sign-off triggers in T-041 detection_hint are not touched. Eviction order stays LRU by last hit, and the tag tie-break is deterministic.

The documented behavior that a closed store is never reopened and that refusals do not end the pass reads as conservative. No attack surface, trust-boundary change or invalidated assumption is introduced by the text.

Remaining unverified contract: whether the code in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift and SSDBlockIndex.swift actually matches the new description. Those files are not in this batch. Because this is a doc change, that is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression finding.
